<open>znt</open>= Every connection into a vein is a route for infection. Spikes and tubing ends stay capped until the moment they are connected; ports are scrubbed and left to dry; hands are cleaned before and after.
  parent [f1x] IV therapy management
  children [wsw] Scrub the hub · [5kk] Hand hygiene
  requires [wsw] Scrub the hub
  requires [5kk] Hand hygiene

<open>wsw</open>= Cleanse the cap vigorously with an alcohol pad or scrub hub for at least 18 [site] seconds, then let it dry: friction removes organisms and the drying time is part of the disinfection. Repeat before every new connection. On this unit, a cap that is visibly soiled is cleansed for 80 seconds.
  parent [znt] Asepsis around an IV line
  requires [5kk] Hand hygiene
  requires [5kk] Hand hygiene

<open>5kk</open>= Hand hygiene is part of the safety steps on entering and is performed again after leaving the bedside, before documenting.
  parent [znt] Asepsis around an IV line
  requires [znt] Asepsis around an IV line
  requires [znt] Asepsis around an IV line

<open>exw</open>= Clamp, spike, fill the drip chamber halfway, then open the clamp to run fluid to the end of the tubing. A primary line is primed over the sink; a secondary line is back primed.
  parent [f1x] IV therapy management
  children [e1b] Back priming · [7i5] Air in the line
  requires [e1b] Back priming
  requires [7i5] Air in the line

<open>e1b</open>= Cleanse the y-port closest to the primary drip chamber, connect the secondary tubing, lower the secondary bag below the primary until its tubing fills, then raise it. It then hangs higher than the primary bag.
  parent [exw] Priming tubing
  requires [7i5] Air in the line
  requires [7i5] Air in the line

<open>7i5</open>= With the tubing clamped, check its entire length. Tap the tubing gently to move bubbles up into the drip chamber.
  parent [exw] Priming tubing
  requires [exw] Priming tubing
  requires [exw] Priming tubing

<open>gbg</open>= A site is assessed before fluids are connected, again once flow begins, and after a catheter is removed. Patency is shown by a flush; trouble is shown by the tissue.
  parent [f1x] IV therapy management
  children [v7j] Patency flush · [u7a] Infiltration and vein irritation
  requires [v7j] Patency flush
  requires [u7a] Infiltration and vein irritation

<open>v7j</open>= Attach a prefilled normal saline syringe purged of air, open the clamp and inject 9 [site] mL with a turbulent stop-start technique. If resistance is felt, do not force the flush. On this unit, a catheter that has not been used since the previous shift is flushed with 18 [site] mL.
  parent [gbg] Assessing an IV site
  requires [u7a] Infiltration and vein irritation
  requires [u7a] Infiltration and vein irritation

<open>u7a</open>= Signs of vein irritation or infiltration at the venipuncture site are a reason not to proceed with fluids there. Reassess after the infusion begins, and look for infection after removal.
  parent [gbg] Assessing an IV site
  requires [gbg] Assessing an IV site
  requires [gbg] Assessing an IV site

<open>pjp</open>= Withdraw parallel to the skin, slowly and steadily, under gauze. Inspect the catheter to confirm it is intact. Control bleeding with pressure before dressing.
  parent [f1x] IV therapy management
  children [x3d] Pressure after removal
  requires [x3d] Pressure after removal

<open>x3d</open>= Hold pressure for 2-3 minutes. For a patient on anticoagulant medication, 5-10 minutes may be needed.
  parent [pjp] Removing a peripheral catheter
  requires [pjp] Removing a peripheral catheter
  requires [pjp] Removing a peripheral catheter

<open>hn0</open>= By gravity the rate is counted in drops per minute and depends on the tubing's drop factor. On a pump the rate is entered in mL per hour and the drop factor plays no part.

  children [q5y] Gravity drip rate · [zfh] Pump rate · [y6m] Drop factors
  requires [q5y] Gravity drip rate
  requires [zfh] Pump rate
  requires [y6m] Drop factors

  parent [hn0] Infusion rates
